summary: Maine's second-oldest light station, on a fog-bound island at the mouth of the Kennebec; its 1857 first-order Fresnel lens still shines.

access.note: Island reached by boat; Friends of Seguin Island open grounds, tower and museum with volunteer keepers in summer.

stay.note: Guest quarters rented to Friends members only, two nights maximum.

notes_for_editor: Corpus has no Light-House Board reports before 1891, so the 1857 build, 1873 whistle and 1889 building rest on LighthouseFriends/NEL/NRHP/USLHS. Conflicts stated in text: first tower date and cost; stone tower 1819 vs 1820; fog hours 2,734 (Bulletin, NRHP, Putnam) vs 2,374 (NEL, likely transposition); focal height 180 ft (NRHP, USLHS) vs 186 ft (LighthouseFriends); Spinney bird count 275 (NEL) vs 500 (LF); oil house 1891 (LF) vs 1892 (USLHS) vs the 1891-92 volume; NRHP lists fog signal building under 1857 vs 1889 elsewhere; Irvine tramway accident accounts differ on which parent saved which child; tramway length 750-1,000+ ft in sources, omitted. 1894 Board report page numbers are scan pages (printed numbers unconfirmed); the report year of that volume is labelled by the corpus as 1893-94. The 1904 Kennebec Journal notice gives no first name for Spinney and says 'fifteen years' as keeper, which the roster does not support; the link to Herbert L. Spinney rests on the initials and station. The Todd 1842 report, Ilsley 1825 letter, Day 1880 letter, 1786 petition and Polereczky letters are quoted second-hand via LighthouseFriends/NEL and footnoted to them. Roster lines (191) come verbatim from the USLHS archive; none matched to other stations. No wreck is tied to Seguin by any source reached. Ghost stories (Thomson via NEL) were left out. Lights characteristic 'F W' from the record. Verifier 2026-10-22: Putnam page 70 and Bulletin 1912 (30 percent) confirmed; 1894 and 1895 Board figures are fiscal years ended June 30; focal height conflict (180 vs 186 ft) and oil-house conflict (NRHP 1857) now stated in text.
